**1 — Scene:** A large leafy salad over or beside a small piece of vegetable-and-cheese pizza.

**2 — Vessel:** White, rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 26 cm across. Using an effective diameter of 26 cm gives an estimated area of **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Mixed salad leaves, a cheese-topped pizza piece, tomato pieces, and a green olive. No separate oil or dressing is clearly visible, so none is added.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area | Height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Mixed leaves | 58% | 308 cm² | 3 cm | 924 ml | 0.13 g/ml | 120 g | 20 | 24 kcal |
| Cheese-and-vegetable pizza | 14% | 74 cm² | 1.3 cm | 96 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 91 g | 270 | 246 kcal |
| Tomato pieces | 5% | 27 cm² | 1.5 cm | 41 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 24 g | 18 | 4 kcal |
| Green olive | 1% | 5 cm² | 1 cm | 5 ml | 0.70 g/ml | 4 g | 145 | 6 kcal |

The allocated areas total **78%** of the plate. Areas are apportioned between items rather than double-counting overlapping leaves and pizza.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **239 g and 280 kcal** is plausible for a voluminous but lightweight salad with a small, denser pizza piece. The pizza identification and any hidden dressing are the largest uncertainties.
